root_cause.text: The CXL mailbox input validator cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() in drivers/cxl/core/mbox.c dereferenced opcode-specific payload structures from user-controlled input without first checking that the supplied in_size was large enough for those casts and field accesses.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() "casts and dereferences the input payload without first verifying its size," and the patch fixes this by adding an in_size parameter plus size checks before accessing struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info and uuid_t, preventing the reported slab-out-of-bounds read in uuid_equal() for an undersized CLEAR_LOG payload.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The CXL mailbox input validator cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() in drivers/cxl/core/mbox.c dereferenced opcode-specific payload structures from user-controlled input without first checking that the supplied in_size was large enough for those casts and field accesses.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly says cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() "casts and dereferences the input payload without first verifying its size," and the patch fixes this by adding an in_size parameter plus size checks before accessing struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info and uuid_t, preventing the reported slab-out-of-bounds read in uuid_equal() for an undersized CLEAR_LOG payload.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document the `in_size` parameter in the kernel-doc for `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: A documentation comment was updated to add a new parameter description line for `@in_size`, stating that it is the size of `@payload_in` in bytes, in the kernel-doc block for `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()`.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it improves the function's documentation so the `in_size` parameter is explicitly described for readers and documentation tooling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an input-size check for SET_PARTITION_INFO payloads so undersized user buffers are rejected before their fields are accessed.
intent_record.what: The function cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() was modified to take an additional size_t in_size parameter, and in the CXL_MBOX_OP_SET_PARTITION_INFO case it now checks whether in_size is smaller than sizeof(struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info) and returns false before accessing the payload fields.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from reading pi->flags from an undersized user-provided input buffer, rejecting malformed SET_PARTITION_INFO payloads early and avoiding out-of-bounds access or use of incomplete data at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a size check for CLEAR_LOG payloads so undersized user input is rejected before reading a UUID.
intent_record.what: In the CXL_MBOX_OP_CLEAR_LOG case of cxl_payload_from_user_allowed(), a new conditional check was added before using payload_in as a uuid_t pointer: if (in_size < sizeof(uuid_t)) return false.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now rejects CLEAR_LOG requests whose input payload is smaller than a UUID, preventing the code from treating an undersized user buffer as a valid uuid_t and avoiding out-of-bounds or invalid access when validating the log identifier.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the input size into user-payload validation so mailbox commands can reject invalid or unsafe input buffers based on length.
intent_record.what: The call to cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() in cxl_mbox_cmd_ctor() was changed to pass a third argument, in_size, with the invocation split across two lines for formatting.
intent_record.how: The payload validation routine now receives the input payload size in addition to the opcode and payload pointer, allowing validation to consider the actual buffer length when deciding whether user-provided input is allowed and potentially rejecting inputs that were previously accepted without size-aware checks.

grouping_result.intent: Document the `in_size` parameter in the kernel-doc for `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` without changing behavior.
Pass the input size into user-payload validation so mailbox commands can reject invalid or unsafe input buffers based on length.

consistency_review.core_intent: Pass input buffer length into mailbox user-payload validation and add per-command size checks so undersized payloads are rejected before fields are accessed.

relevance_review.reason: The change only updates kernel-doc to mention `in_size` and does not add the missing size checks before dereferencing user-controlled payload structures, so it does not address the vulnerability root cause.
The changes directly address the root cause by passing in_size to the validator and adding opcode-specific minimum-size checks before casting/accessing payload fields from user-controlled input.

candidates.rationale: This casts user-controlled input to an opcode-specific structure without first verifying that the supplied input buffer is large enough for that structure, enabling subsequent field dereference on undersized input.
This dereferences a field from the casted user payload without a prior size check, directly embodying the out-of-bounds read risk on undersized buffers.
This treats user-controlled input as a UUID pointer without validating that the input length is at least sizeof(uuid_t), setting up an unsafe dereference.
This call site invokes validation without passing the input length, preventing opcode-specific checks from rejecting undersized payloads before structure casts and field accesses occur.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement casts user-controlled input to an opcode-specific structure before verifying that the supplied input buffer is large enough, which is the root cause of the unsafe dereference on undersized payloads.
This statement dereferences a field from the structure obtained from user-controlled input without a prior input-size check, directly triggering the out-of-bounds read condition on short buffers.
This statement interprets user-controlled input as a UUID pointer without first ensuring the input is at least sizeof(uuid_t), enabling unsafe subsequent access to undersized payload data.

This call site performs validation without supplying the user input length, preventing the validator from rejecting undersized opcode-specific payloads before the later casts and field dereferences occur.

Author: Alison Schofield <alison.schofield@intel.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 30 18:27:18 2022 -0700

    cxl/mbox: Block immediate mode in SET_PARTITION_INFO command
    
    User space may send the SET_PARTITION_INFO mailbox command using
    the IOCTL interface. Inspect the input payload and fail if the
    immediate flag is set.
    
    This is the first instance of the driver inspecting an input payload
    from user space. Assume there will be more
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the entire new helper `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` and its call site in `cxl_mbox_cmd_ctor()`, which is exactly where the user-controlled payload is inspected. The vulnerable construct is present: `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed(u16 opcode, void *payload_in)` takes only `payload_in` and no `in_size`, so it has no way to validate that the buffer is large enough before opcode-specific casting and dereference. In the `CXL_MBOX_OP_SET_PARTITION_INFO` case it does `struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info *pi = payload_in;` and then immediately accesses `pi->flags` in `if (pi->flags && CXL_SET_PARTITION_IMMEDIATE_FLAG)`, which is a dereference of an opcode-specific structure from user-controlled input without first checking the supplied input length. The call site confirms no size-based validation occurs before inspection: after copying `in_payload` with `memdup_user()` using `in_size`, the code directly calls `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed(opcode, mbox->payload_in)`. Since the helper is not passed `in_size`, the fix for the root cause is not present.
